what_this_is: What the machines are doing right now. Each count is read from the file that job writes as it works, not typed in by hand. Nothing here is a result. Results go to the data page when the job that produced them finishes.

jobs.title: Does a structure help when almost nothing has been measured
jobs.note: 32 further proteins were declined, because their measured compounds do not spread across enough distinct chemistry to split into a held-out set. The registration asks for 25 or as many as exist.
jobs.why_it_matters: This is the claim the product rests on. If a model trained only on known actives wins here, the claim is withdrawn.
jobs.link_text: the registration, written before any result

jobs.title: Searching every protein in ChEMBL for ones nobody has measured
jobs.note: 53 qualify so far. A protein qualifies with 15 to 45 measured compounds and 150 to 420 residues, which is few enough that a model trained on known actives has almost nothing to learn from.
jobs.why_it_matters: The experiment above cannot finish until this finds enough proteins, so this is the thing holding it up.

jobs.title: Rescoring every published protein under the corrected pipeline
jobs.note: Every figure on this site was computed before two defects were fixed. This recomputes all of them to find out whether the published numbers move. Whatever it returns goes on the site, including if it goes against us.
jobs.why_it_matters: If the headline moves, the headline changes and the old one stays in the corrections record.

jobs.title: Does folding a complex beat a random forest on fingerprints
jobs.verdict: the ligand model wins, minus 0.1445, interval minus 0.191 to minus 0.0992
jobs.note: Three arms on the same held-out compounds. The structure predictions already recorded, a random forest trained on the ChEMBL pool with those compounds removed, and the rank average of the two with nothing fitted. Finished at 121 of 123. Two targets carry fewer than five compounds with both a prediction and a measurement and were excluded by a floor that predates the run.
jobs.why_it_matters: This is the control that could take the corpus number off the front page. If the ligand arm wins across the corpus, folding is not what produces the ranking.
jobs.link_text: the result, and the rule it fired

jobs.title: Ranking inside the 1.5 log window a chemist works in
jobs.verdict: the ligand model wins inside the window, minus 0.1436, interval minus 0.2265 to minus 0.0625
jobs.note: Our headline is measured on held-out sets spanning four log units of potency. A medicinal chemist works inside one and a half. This scores both arms again with the range held fixed, on predictions already on disk, so it costs no GPU time. A timer reruns it every 30 minutes as the remaining ChEMBL pools arrive, so between firings it is armed rather than working.
jobs.why_it_matters: This is the first question a medicinal chemist asks, and it had never been measured here.

jobs.title: Finding known actives hidden in a library of 5,000
jobs.note: Each library holds 50 known actives among 4,950 decoys matched on weight and logP. A fingerprint prefilter ranks all 5,000 and the top 150 are folded and re-ranked. The prefilter alone is the control.
jobs.why_it_matters: If the prefilter and the funnel enrich equally, the expensive stage is decoration and the registration says we publish that.
